note: Unit prices for the four lines that make up a voice-agent call. Every number carries the vendor page it came from and the date it was read. This file is the data layer; voicecost.py is the only renderer.
disclosure: Links marked affiliate are a9n9's affiliate links: a9n9 earns a commission if you buy through them. The buyer pays the vendor's own price; nothing is returned to the buyer.

elevenlabs.name: ElevenLabs
elevenlabs.affiliate_disclosure: affiliate link: a9n9 earns a commission if you buy through it
elevenlabs.agent_note: Agents, Realtime v1 Mini and Realtime v1 Max are all printed as $0.08 per minute. On the two Realtime tiers the page adds '+ LLM usage', i.e. the LLM is a separate bill there.
elevenlabs.ladder_note: Characters included per month at list price. The ladder is flat at ~$1 per 12,500 characters, so a bigger plan does not lower the unit price; above 12,375,000 characters/month the published self-serve ladder ends.
traps: The marketing FAQ describes credits ($0.18 per 1,000 characters) while /pricing/api bills dollars ($0.08 per 1,000) - a 2.3x difference depending on which page you read.
First-month promos are not prices: list price is $6 Starter / $22 Creator.

deepgram.name: Deepgram
traps: The $0.075 headline on that page is the Voice Agent (STT + managed LLM + TTS), not speech-to-text. STT alone is $0.0043-$0.0092 per minute, i.e. 8-17x cheaper; reading the agent rate as an STT rate is the single most common pricing error about Deepgram.
Deepgram is not an affiliate partner of a9n9: no link, no commission. It appears here because it is the cheapest line in the stack, and a comparison that hid it would be an advertisement.

novita.name: Novita AI
novita.affiliate_disclosure: affiliate link: a9n9 earns a commission if you buy through it
traps: The model, not the provider, sets this line. The same model id is sold by other providers at up to 7.6x the price, so re-check the model id before quoting it.

telephony.name: Telephony (carrier)
telephony.source: not a vendor page: a default the user should replace with their carrier's rate
traps: Inbound and outbound numbers, per-minute termination and number rental are three different charges on a real phone bill. This line is one number for all three; it is an estimate, not a quote.

managed-el.name: ElevenLabs Agents (managed)
managed-el.what: One vendor bills one price per connected minute: speech recognition, a managed LLM and speech synthesis are inside it.

dg-agent.name: Deepgram Voice Agent (managed)
dg-agent.what: Deepgram's bundled agent minute: STT + managed LLM + TTS.

assembled.name: Assembled cheap stack
assembled.what: Deepgram streaming STT + Novita open-model LLM + Deepgram Aura-2 TTS, billed separately. Cheapest of the four, and the most work to operate.

el-tts.name: ElevenLabs TTS + cheap STT and LLM
el-tts.what: ElevenLabs voice quality on the output side, priced per character, with recognition and the LLM bought elsewhere.

assumptions.chars_per_spoken_minute_note: Characters of script per minute of finished audio swings 600-1,000 with speaker and pacing. ElevenLabs' own price table divides by 1,000 ('75,000 chars ~ 75 min'); 900 is used here as a middle estimate and every number moves with it.
assumptions.tokens_note: A 3-minute call at 2 turns per minute is 6 turns; 250 input tokens per turn is a short system prompt plus the last few exchanges, 45 out is one or two spoken sentences.
